title: slacheck: availability commitments for distributed applications
tagline: Check an availability objective and find the smallest single-service repair.
problem: A service-level objective can exceed what its required dependencies deliver.
approach: A reduced decision diagram evaluates required and alternative dependencies, counts each shared service once and solves the minimum conditional thresholds.

demo.caption: Check an infeasible shop objective, then print its highest-ranked repair.

results.label: Infeasible commitments detected
results.setup: 72 synthetic graphs, six seeds, separate held-out family, exhaustive oracle.

results.label: Slowest 200-service CLI run
results.setup: Two graphs, seven serial runs each. CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor (x86_64); Python 3.10.12; no GPU.

limits: The exact calculation assumes independent failure states for distinct services.
Trace imports do not infer redundancy or local service availability.
The repair ranking changes one service at a time.
role: Sole developer. Built during my ML research internship at Devoteam (AIOps), where it is used internally. Co-author of the accompanying research, which I presented in the ISSRE 2026 industry session.
